statement: A fixed scale at or below every observation gives the threshold limit. Each observation equal to the scale contributes a factor of one half.
hypotheses_and_conclusion:
{x : Fin n → ℝ} {a k : ℝ} (ha : 0 < a)
    (hk : 0 < k) (hx : ∀ i, a ≤ x i) :
    Tendsto (fun b : ℝ ↦ ShapeFacesPGW.logLik x b a (k / b)) atTop
      (𝓝 (thresholdLogLik x a k))

statement: At or below the minimum, each finite density loses to the threshold density at the same product of shape and exponent.
hypotheses_and_conclusion:
{a x b k : ℝ} (ha : 0 < a)
    (hx : a ≤ x) (hb : 0 < b) (hk : 0 < k) :
    ShapeFacesPGW.logDensity b a (k / b) x <
      log k - log x - (if x = a then log 2 else 0) +
        k * log (x / a) - (exp (k * log (x / a)) - 1)

statement: A positive held scale at or below all observations has no finite maximizer. This includes constant samples and ties at the scale.
hypotheses_and_conclusion:
(hn : 0 < n) {x : Fin n → ℝ} {a : ℝ}
    (ha : 0 < a) (hx : ∀ i, a ≤ x i) :
    ¬ ∃ p ∈ Weibull.domain,
      IsMaxOn (fun q : ℝ × ℝ ↦ ShapeFacesPGW.logLik x q.1 a q.2) Weibull.domain p

statement: The power-transformed Gompertz face along a path with fixed shape.
hypotheses_and_conclusion:
{x : Fin n → ℝ} {b r : ℝ} (hb : 0 < b) (hr : 0 < r)
    (hx : ∀ i, 0 < x i) :
    Tendsto (fun h : ℝ ↦ ShapeFacesPGW.logLik x b ((h * r) ^ (-1 / b)) h⁻¹)
      (𝓝[>] 0) (𝓝 (gompertzLogLik x b r))

statement: The cumulative hazard on the fixed-scale threshold path, on both sides of the threshold and at equality.
hypotheses_and_conclusion:
{x a k : ℝ} (hx : 0 < x) (ha : 0 < a) (hk : 0 < k) :
    Tendsto (fun b : ℝ ↦ (1 + (x / a) ^ b) ^ (k / b) - 1) atTop
      (𝓝 (if a ≤ x then (x / a) ^ k - 1 else 0))

statement: Constants strictly below the held scale concentrate by sending the shape to infinity and taking the reciprocal powered ratio as exponent.
hypotheses_and_conclusion:
{a x : ℝ} (hn : 0 < n) (hx : 0 < x) (ha : x < a) :
    Tendsto (fun b : ℝ ↦ ShapeFacesPGW.logLik (fun _ : Fin n ↦ x)
      b a ((x / a) ^ b)⁻¹) atTop atTop

statement: At a held positive shape, a powered observation-to-maximum ratio at least one half for every observation excludes every finite maximizer.
hypotheses_and_conclusion:
(hn : 0 < n) {x : Fin n → ℝ} {b X : ℝ}
    (hb : 0 < b) (hx : ∀ i, 0 < x i) (hX : ∀ i, x i ≤ X)
    (hnarrow : ∀ i, 1 / 2 ≤ (x i / X) ^ b) :
    ¬ ∃ p ∈ Weibull.domain,
      IsMaxOn (fun q : ℝ × ℝ ↦ ShapeFacesPGW.logLik x b q.1 q.2) Weibull.domain p

statement: For nonconstant data with a held scale above some observation, joint optimization over the shape and exponent attains a finite maximum.
hypotheses_and_conclusion:
{x : Fin n → ℝ} {a : ℝ} (ha : 0 < a)
    (hx : ∀ i, 0 < x i) {i j : Fin n} (hij : x i < x j) (hia : x i < a) :
    ∃ p ∈ Weibull.domain,
      IsMaxOn (fun q : ℝ × ℝ ↦ ShapeFacesPGW.logLik x q.1 a q.2) Weibull.domain p

statement: Holding the scale leaves a finite maximizer exactly for nonconstant positive data with an observation strictly below the scale.
hypotheses_and_conclusion:
(hn : 0 < n) {x : Fin n → ℝ} {a : ℝ}
    (ha : 0 < a) (hx : ∀ i, 0 < x i) :
    (∃ p ∈ Weibull.domain,
      IsMaxOn (fun q : ℝ × ℝ ↦ ShapeFacesPGW.logLik x q.1 a q.2) Weibull.domain p) ↔
      (∃ i j, x i ≠ x j) ∧ ∃ i, x i < a

statement: With shape held, a finite fit attains exactly when some finite witness ties or beats every Gompertz likelihood. The witness need not beat the face strictly.
hypotheses_and_conclusion:
{x : Fin n → ℝ} (hn : 0 < n)
    (hx : ∀ i, 0 < x i) {b : ℝ} (hb : 0 < b) :
    (∃ p ∈ Weibull.domain,
      IsMaxOn (fun q : ℝ × ℝ ↦ ShapeFacesPGW.logLik x b q.1 q.2) Weibull.domain p) ↔
      ∃ a > 0, ∃ c > 0, ∀ r > 0, gompertzLogLik x b r ≤ ShapeFacesPGW.logLik x b a c

statement: The held-shape criterion can be tested at finite stationary points. The nonstrict face comparison preserves finite equality.
hypotheses_and_conclusion:
{x : Fin n → ℝ} (hn : 0 < n)
    (hx : ∀ i, 0 < x i) {b : ℝ} (hb : 0 < b) :
    (∃ p ∈ Weibull.domain,
      IsMaxOn (fun q : ℝ × ℝ ↦ ShapeFacesPGW.logLik x b q.1 q.2) Weibull.domain p) ↔
      ∃ a > 0, ∃ c > 0,
        deriv (fun s ↦ ShapeFacesPGW.logLik x b s c) a = 0 ∧
        deriv (ShapeFacesPGW.logLik x b a) c = 0 ∧
        ∀ r > 0, gompertzLogLik x b r ≤ ShapeFacesPGW.logLik x b a c

statement: The threshold face has a unique positive exponent whenever at least one observation lies strictly above the held threshold.
hypotheses_and_conclusion:
{x : Fin n → ℝ} {a : ℝ} (ha : 0 < a)
    (hx : ∀ i, a ≤ x i) (hne : ∃ i, a < x i) :
    ∃! k, k ∈ Ioi (0 : ℝ) ∧ IsMaxOn (thresholdLogLik x a) (Ioi 0) k

statement: The power-transformed Gompertz face has a unique optimizing scale at each positive held shape, even on constant data.
hypotheses_and_conclusion:
(hn : 0 < n) {x : Fin n → ℝ} (hx : ∀ i, 0 < x i)
    {b : ℝ} :
    ∃! r, r ∈ Ioi (0 : ℝ) ∧ IsMaxOn (gompertzLogLik x b) (Ioi 0) r

statement: The optimized threshold likelihood is the strict all-free-in-shape-and- exponent supremum when the fixed scale is at or below the minimum and some observation is strictly above the scale.
hypotheses_and_conclusion:
(hn : 0 < n) {x : Fin n → ℝ} {a : ℝ}
    (ha : 0 < a) (hx : ∀ i, a ≤ x i) (hne : ∃ i, a < x i) :
    ∃ k > 0,
      IsLUB ((fun p : ℝ × ℝ ↦ ShapeFacesPGW.logLik x p.1 a p.2) '' Weibull.domain)
        (thresholdLogLik x a k) ∧
      ∀ p ∈ Weibull.domain, ShapeFacesPGW.logLik x p.1 a p.2 < thresholdLogLik x a k

statement: The cumulative hazard on the fixed-shape Gompertz path converges at every positive observation.
hypotheses_and_conclusion:
{b r x : ℝ} (hb : 0 < b) (hr : 0 < r) (hx : 0 < x) :
    Tendsto (fun h : ℝ ↦ (1 + (x / (h * r) ^ (-1 / b)) ^ b) ^ h⁻¹ - 1)
      (𝓝[>] 0) (𝓝 (exp (r * x ^ b) - 1))

statement: With scale free, approaching the threshold from below at log distance `h` while shape grows as `h⁻²` attains the unpenalized endpoint likelihood.
hypotheses_and_conclusion:
{x : Fin n → ℝ} {a k : ℝ} (ha : 0 < a)
    (hk : 0 < k) (hx : ∀ i, a ≤ x i) :
    Tendsto (fun h : ℝ ↦ ShapeFacesPGW.logLik x (h^2)⁻¹ (a * exp (-h)) (k * h^2))
      (𝓝[>] 0) (𝓝 (∑ i, (log k - log (x i) + k * log (x i / a) -
        (exp (k * log (x i / a)) - 1))))

statement: The free scale approaches the endpoint while leaving zero exponential loss even for observations tied at the endpoint.
hypotheses_and_conclusion:
{x : Fin n → ℝ} {A d : ℝ} (hd : 0 < d) (_hA : 0 < A)
    (hx : ∀ i, 0 < x i ∧ x i ≤ A) :
    Tendsto (fun q : ℝ ↦ TransformedGamma.logLik x (d * q) q⁻¹
      (exp (log A - q * log q))) (𝓝[>] 0)
      (𝓝 (log d - Gamma.avgLog x + Gamma.avg (fun i ↦ d * (log (x i) - log A))))

statement: The reciprocal path gives the Pareto log likelihood, including lower-endpoint ties.
hypotheses_and_conclusion:
{x : Fin n → ℝ} {A d : ℝ} (hd : 0 < d) (hA : 0 < A)
    (hx : ∀ i, A ≤ x i) :
    Tendsto (fun q : ℝ ↦ InverseTransformedGamma.logLik x (d * q) q⁻¹
      (exp (log A⁻¹ - q * log q))⁻¹) (𝓝[>] 0)
      (𝓝 (log d - Gamma.avgLog x + Gamma.avg (fun i ↦ d * (log A - log (x i)))))

statement: Integer gamma shapes tending to infinity give a lognormal likelihood path at any fixed log location and positive log scale.
hypotheses_and_conclusion:
(hn : 0 < n) (x : Fin n → ℝ) (μ : ℝ) {σ : ℝ} (hσ : 0 < σ) :
    Tendsto (fun j : ℕ ↦ TransformedGamma.logLik x j (1 / (σ * sqrt j))
      (exp (μ - log j * (σ * sqrt j)))) atTop
      (𝓝 (Gamma.avg (fun i ↦ -log σ - log (2 * π) / 2 - log (x i) -
        ((log (x i) - μ) / σ)^2 / 2)))

statement: Reciprocation gives the lognormal likelihood at reflected log location.
hypotheses_and_conclusion:
(hn : 0 < n) (x : Fin n → ℝ) (μ : ℝ)
    {σ : ℝ} (hσ : 0 < σ) :
    Tendsto (fun j : ℕ ↦ InverseTransformedGamma.logLik x j (1 / (σ * sqrt j))
      (exp (-μ - log j * (σ * sqrt j)))⁻¹) atTop
      (𝓝 (Gamma.avg (fun i ↦ -log σ - log (2 * π) / 2 - log (x i) -
        ((log (x i) - μ) / σ)^2 / 2)))

statement: When the mean gap to the supported endpoint in oriented log units is positive, its reciprocal is the unique rate optimizing the face.
hypotheses_and_conclusion:
{D : ℝ} (hD : 0 < D) :
    ∃! d, d ∈ Set.Ioi (0 : ℝ) ∧
      IsMaxOn (fun r ↦ log r - r * D) (Set.Ioi 0) d

statement: With location equal to the common log observation, taking scale to zero makes log likelihood unbounded for every fixed shape, including zero.
hypotheses_and_conclusion:
{n : ℕ} (hn : 0 < n) (μ Q : ℝ)
    {x : Fin n → ℝ} (hx : ∀ i, x i = exp μ) :
    Tendsto (fun σ : ℝ ↦ GenGammaTwoPoint.sampleLogLik x (μ, σ, Q))
      (𝓝[>] 0) atTop

statement: With location equal to the common log observation, taking scale to zero makes log likelihood unbounded for every fixed shape, including zero.
hypotheses_and_conclusion:
{n : ℕ} (hn : 0 < n) (μ Q : ℝ)
    {x : Fin n → ℝ} (hx : ∀ i, x i = exp μ) :
    Tendsto (fun σ : ℝ ↦ GenGammaTwoPoint.sampleLogLik x (μ, σ, Q))
      (𝓝[>] 0) atTop

statement: For either orientation, the fixed-location path tends to the power or Pareto log likelihood when all observations are on the supported side. At zero residual the exponential loss still vanishes.
hypotheses_and_conclusion:
{n : ℕ} {x : Fin n → ℝ} {μ d : ℝ}
    (hd : 0 < d) (ε : ℝ) (hε : |ε| = 1)
    (hx : ∀ i, ε * (log (x i) - μ) ≤ 0) :
    Tendsto (fun q : ℝ ↦ GenGammaTwoPoint.sampleLogLik x
      (μ, d * sqrt q, ε / sqrt q)) (𝓝[>] 0)
      (𝓝 ((∑ i, (-log d + ε * (log (x i) - μ) / d - log (x i))) / n))

statement: For either orientation, the fixed-location path tends to the power or Pareto log likelihood when all observations are on the supported side. At zero residual the exponential loss still vanishes.
hypotheses_and_conclusion:
{n : ℕ} {x : Fin n → ℝ} {μ d : ℝ}
    (hd : 0 < d) (ε : ℝ) (hε : |ε| = 1)
    (hx : ∀ i, ε * (log (x i) - μ) ≤ 0) :
    Tendsto (fun q : ℝ ↦ GenGammaTwoPoint.sampleLogLik x
      (μ, d * sqrt q, ε / sqrt q)) (𝓝[>] 0)
      (𝓝 ((∑ i, (-log d + ε * (log (x i) - μ) / d - log (x i))) / n))

statement: At fixed location and fixed real shape, any nonzero log residual gives a unique positive scale maximizer, including the normal shape.
hypotheses_and_conclusion:
{n : ℕ} (hn : 0 < n) {x : Fin n → ℝ} (μ Q : ℝ)
    (hne : ∃ i, log (x i) ≠ μ) :
    ∃! σ, σ ∈ Ioi (0 : ℝ) ∧
      IsMaxOn (fun s ↦ GenGammaTwoPoint.sampleLogLik x (μ, s, Q)) (Ioi 0) σ

statement: Inversion exchanges the two shapes and inverts the scale.
hypotheses_and_conclusion:
{x : Fin n → ℝ} (hx : ∀ i, 0 < x i)
    {b : ℝ} (hb : 0 < b) (p q : ℝ) :
    BetaPrime.logLik x b (p, q) =
      BetaPrime.logLik (fun i ↦ (x i)⁻¹) b⁻¹ (q, p) - ∑ i, 2 * log (x i)

statement: Constant data have unbounded beta-prime likelihood even at any fixed positive scale.
At any fixed positive first shape, sending the second shape and scale to infinity at fixed ratio gives the corresponding gamma likelihood.
hypotheses_and_conclusion:
{x : Fin n → ℝ} (hx : ∀ i, 0 < x i)
    {s p : ℝ} (hs : 0 < s) (hp : 0 < p) :
    Tendsto (fun h : ℝ ↦ BetaPrime.logLik x (s / h) (p, h⁻¹))
      (𝓝[>] 0) (𝓝 (∑ i, Gamma.logDensity p s⁻¹ (x i)))

statement: At any fixed positive second shape, reciprocal symmetry gives the inverse-gamma likelihood as the first shape diverges and scale decreases.
hypotheses_and_conclusion:
{x : Fin n → ℝ} (hx : ∀ i, 0 < x i)
    {s q : ℝ} (hs : 0 < s) (hq : 0 < q) :
    Tendsto (fun h : ℝ ↦ BetaPrime.logLik x (h / s) (h⁻¹, q))
      (𝓝[>] 0)
      (𝓝 ((∑ i, Gamma.logDensity q s⁻¹ (x i)⁻¹) - ∑ i, 2 * log (x i)))

statement: Every nonempty sample has unbounded likelihood if shapes below minus one are allowed. An attained sample maximum may have any multiplicity.
hypotheses_and_conclusion:
(hn : 0 < n) (x : Fin n → ℝ) :
    ¬ BddAbove {v | ∃ ξ : ℝ, ∃ p ∈ GEV.domain x ξ, GEV.logLik x ξ p = v}

statement: On the fitted branch, a strict majority at the minimum suffices for unboundedness along shape one. Constants are included.
At equal minimum and nonminimum counts, the shape-one path tends to the stated finite total log likelihood. The lower endpoint stays strictly below the minimum at finite parameters.
hypotheses_and_conclusion:
(hn : 0 < n) {x : Fin n → ℝ} {m : ℝ}
    (hm : ∀ i, m ≤ x i) (hz : ∃ i, x i = m)
    (hc : n = 2 * Frechet.minimumCount (GEV.lowerGaps x m)) :
    (∀ e > 0, GEV.collapsePath x m 1 e ∈ GEV.domain x 1) ∧
    Tendsto (GEV.collapsePath x m 1) (𝓝[>] 0) (𝓝 (m, 0)) ∧
    Tendsto (fun e ↦ GEV.logLik x 1 (GEV.collapsePath x m 1 e)) (𝓝[>] 0)
      (𝓝 ((n : ℝ) * (log 2 - 1) - 2 * ∑ i, log (x i - m)))

statement: Keep `σ / λ = a` and `μ + σ = b` as shape diverges. The Fréchet log likelihood converges to Gumbel at the same location and scale.
hypotheses_and_conclusion:
(x : Fin n → ℝ) (m b : ℝ) {a : ℝ} (ha : 0 < a) :
    Tendsto (fun h : ℝ ↦ Frechet.logLik (GEV.lowerGaps x m) h⁻¹ (m - b + a / h) (a / h))
      (𝓝[>] 0) (𝓝 (GEV.logLik x 0 (b, a)))

statement: Allowing all positive shapes makes the likelihood unbounded whenever the nonnegative gaps include a zero. A small fixed shape already suffices.
The product of two Fréchet densities at distance `d` is strictly below the half-minimum collapse bound on the fitted shape branch.
hypotheses_and_conclusion:
{a s e d : ℝ} (ha : 1 ≤ a) (hs : 0 < s)
    (he : 0 < e) (hd : 0 < d) :
    Frechet.logDensity a s e + Frechet.logDensity a s (e + d) <
      2 * (log 2 - 1 - log d)

statement: At exactly half minimum multiplicity the fitted Fréchet likelihood has a finite strict supremum, approached along shape one.
hypotheses_and_conclusion:
{g : Fin n → ℝ} (hn : 0 < n)
    (hg : ∀ i, 0 ≤ g i) (hc : n = 2 * Frechet.minimumCount g) :
    let A := (n : ℝ) * (log 2 - 1) - 2 * ∑ i, log (g i)
    IsLUB {v | ∃ a ≥ 1, ∃ p ∈ Frechet.domain, Frechet.logLik g a p.1 p.2 = v} A ∧
    (∀ a ≥ 1, ∀ p ∈ Frechet.domain, Frechet.logLik g a p.1 p.2 < A) ∧
    Tendsto (Frechet.profile g 1) (𝓝[>] 0) (𝓝 A)

statement: A strict majority of minimum observations causes divergence on the fitted branch, already at Fréchet shape one.
hypotheses_and_conclusion:
{g : Fin n → ℝ} (hn : 0 < n)
    (hg : ∀ i, 0 ≤ g i) (hz : ∃ i, g i = 0)
    (hc : n < 2 * Frechet.minimumCount g) :
    ¬ BddAbove {v | ∃ a ≥ 1, ∃ p ∈ Frechet.domain, Frechet.logLik g a p.1 p.2 = v}

statement: With both coefficients free, the all-zero likelihood has supremum one, which no positive finite parameter pair reaches.
hypotheses_and_conclusion:
{n : ℕ} (hn : 0 < n) :
    IsLUB {v | ∃ a > 0, ∃ r > 0,
      Discrete3DGamma.likelihood (fun _ : Fin n ↦ 0) a r = v} 1 ∧
    ∀ a > 0, ∀ r > 0, Discrete3DGamma.likelihood (fun _ : Fin n ↦ 0) a r < 1

statement: Two adjacent cells together have strictly less than unit probability at every finite positive parameter pair, including the cells zero and one.
hypotheses_and_conclusion:
{a r : ℝ} (ha : 0 < a) (hr : 0 < r) (j : ℕ) :
    Discrete3DGamma.cellProb a r j + Discrete3DGamma.cellProb a r (j + 1) < 1

statement: Keep the latent mean strictly inside a specified cell as shape tends to infinity. The fitted mass of that cell converges to one.
hypotheses_and_conclusion:
(j : ℕ) {m : ℝ} (hm : (j : ℝ) < m) (hm' : m < j + 1) :
    Tendsto (fun a : ℝ ↦ Discrete3DGamma.cellProb a (a / m) j) atTop (𝓝 1)

statement: The all-free supremum for a constant count is one, including when the common count is positive. No finite shape and rate attain it.
hypotheses_and_conclusion:
{n : ℕ} (hn : 0 < n) (j : ℕ) :
    IsLUB {v | ∃ a > 0, ∃ r > 0,
      Discrete3DGamma.likelihood (fun _ : Fin n ↦ j) a r = v} 1 ∧
    ∀ a > 0, ∀ r > 0, Discrete3DGamma.likelihood (fun _ : Fin n ↦ j) a r < 1

statement: For two adjacent cells, a rate chosen to give the prescribed CDF at their shared endpoint realizes arbitrary positive limiting proportions.
hypotheses_and_conclusion:
(j : ℕ) {w : ℝ} (hw : w ∈ Ioo (0 : ℝ) 1) :
    ∃ r : ℝ → ℝ, (∀ᶠ a in atTop, 0 < r a) ∧
      Tendsto (fun a ↦ a / r a) atTop (𝓝 ((j : ℝ) + 1)) ∧
      Tendsto (fun a ↦ Discrete3DGamma.cellProb a (r a) j) atTop (𝓝 w) ∧
      Tendsto (fun a ↦ Discrete3DGamma.cellProb a (r a) (j + 1)) atTop (𝓝 (1 - w))

statement: The excluded saturated supremum for counts from two adjacent cells is the product of the empirical cell proportions, with their multiplicities.
hypotheses_and_conclusion:
{n : ℕ} (x : Fin n → ℕ) (j : ℕ)
    (hx : ∀ i, x i = j ∨ x i = j + 1)
    (hl : ∃ i, x i = j) (hu : ∃ i, x i = j + 1) :
    let m := (Finset.univ.filter fun i ↦ x i = j).card
    let k := (Finset.univ.filter fun i ↦ x i ≠ j).card
    let w := (m : ℝ) / (m + k)
    IsLUB {v | ∃ a > 0, ∃ r > 0, Discrete3DGamma.likelihood x a r = v}
      (w ^ m * (1 - w) ^ k) ∧
    ∀ a > 0, ∀ r > 0, Discrete3DGamma.likelihood x a r < w ^ m * (1 - w) ^ k

statement: Two occupied cells separated by at least one cell force a compact positive-likelihood superlevel, yielding a finite joint maximizer.
hypotheses_and_conclusion:
{n : ℕ} {x : Fin n → ℕ} {i j : Fin n} (hij : x i + 1 < x j) :
    ∃ a > 0, ∃ r > 0, ∀ b > 0, ∀ t > 0,
      Discrete3DGamma.likelihood x b t ≤ Discrete3DGamma.likelihood x a r

statement: A nonempty count sample has a finite all-free fit exactly when its integer range is at least two. Zero counts and multiplicities are retained.
hypotheses_and_conclusion:
{n : ℕ} (hn : 0 < n) (x : Fin n → ℕ) :
    (∃ a > 0, ∃ r > 0, ∀ b > 0, ∀ t > 0,
      Discrete3DGamma.likelihood x b t ≤ Discrete3DGamma.likelihood x a r) ↔
      ∃ i j, x i + 1 < x j
